game: LAC@SEA Week 4 2026 (kickoff morning; spread/total not saved; weather not saved)

script.base: No spread or total was saved, so the script is form-only. Seattle's pass game is the engine (Jaxon Smith-Njigba 36 targets, 405 yards in 3 games) against a Chargers defense that has allowed 9 passes of 20+ and 9.47 YPA on the left, with CB Donte Jackson, S Derwin James and S Elijah Molden all questionable. LAC will try to stay on schedule with Omarion Hampton (50 carries, 193 yards) but Seattle allows 3.37 YPC. Most likely flow: Seattle moves it through JSN, game leans Seattle by the second half without a saved number to call it a blowout, LAC rush efficiency is capped, and with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price both out the late carries, if Seattle leads, fall to Emanuel Wilson and George Holani.
script.flip1: Seattle jumps out early. JSN can still clear before the clock-kill, but late WR snaps shrink, Wilson/Holani carries rise, and LAC abandons Hampton (the DAL-style stall). Herbert is then in a bad dropback script (LAC EPA/db -0.46 vs blitz, -0.03 vs none) even though Seattle blitzes only 20%.
script.flip2: Hampton controls the clock and the game becomes a lower-event slog: JSN's 12-target pace dies and the receiving over loses despite the leaky secondary. The other flip is a shootout if LAC's wounded DBs bust, which would lift Tre Harris (20/53/76) with JSN and threaten any LAC receiving under.

injury_fallout: SEA RB Zach Charbonnet Out (knee) and Jadarian Price Out (chest) per the pre-game nflverse report. Price had 28 carries/119 yards beside Wilson 32/109 and Holani 15/52, so that work redistributes to Wilson and Holani; neither line looks fully repriced (see pro_edge). LAC G Kayode Awosika Out (fibula): pressure up, LAC rush efficiency down for Hampton and Keaton Mitchell. LAC DT Dalvin Tomlinson Out (hamstring): small hole in a run defense that already allows 4.00 YPC. LAC WR Ladd McConkey Questionable (foot), not out: if he sits, Harris (16 targets/149 yards) and Quentin Johnston (17 targets but only 64 yards) plus David Njoku (8/67) and Oronde Gadsden (7/50) absorb targets; do not treat that as confirmed. LAC TE Charlie Kolar Out and WR Brenen Thompson Out were not in the week 1-3 target list, so no new fallout. LAC CB/S cluster (Jackson, James, Molden) all Questionable, which would further thin the secondary JSN attacks. SEA LB Chazz Surratt and S Ty Okada Questionable. Trey Lance Questionable is the backup QB, not the starter.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart saved. Proxy is location YPA: Seattle is tight on every side (left 5.78 on 40 attempts, middle 4.93 on 14, right 4.11 on 38) with 2 passes of 20+. LAC is soft outside (left 9.47 on 38, right 7.93 on 30) and only relatively better in the middle (5.67 on 24), with 9 passes of 20+.
matchup.pressure: Seattle blitz rate 20%, so it mostly avoids the down where LAC is worst (EPA/db -0.46 vs blitz, -0.03 vs none). LAC blitzes 25%, and Seattle is better when blitzed (EPA/db +0.47 vs blitz, +0.15 vs none), so pressure helps Seattle's pass game rather than killing JSN's deep/intermediate yards.
matchup.bleeds: LAC bleeds explosive and outside passing, plus a 4.00 YPC run defense (8 runs of 10+) with Tomlinson out. Seattle does not bleed through the air (sub-6 YPA, 2 explosives) and is the stingy run unit (3.37 YPC, 5 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: Seattle's primary target is JSN (36 targets, 405 yards, 348 air yards), and that overlaps the exact leak: LAC outside/explosive passing with three DBs questionable. LAC's air-yards receiver Johnston (171 air yards, 64 receiving yards, 3.8 yards/target) overlaps Seattle's strongest trait, a defense that has not given up explosives.

Johnston 17, 7, 40 despite 171 air yards. McConkey 82, 35, 66 but questionable. Mitchell rush 9, 24, 52 on 17 carries vs Hampton's 50 (52 may be one-play inflation). Herbert rush 29, 2, 17. That JSN counter is weaker than a 122-yard floor and a 36-target role. The Johnston counter is real enough to keep the leg a lean and to scratch it if inactives make him, not Harris, the McConkey replacement.
